rules.title: Machine-wide logon program can be overwritten
rules.subject: {hive}\{name}
rules.why: HKLM Run entries start in every user's session at logon, administrators included. Anyone who can overwrite the program runs code as the next person to log on.
rules.fix: Restrict the program's ACL so only SYSTEM and Administrators can write it, or reinstall it under Program Files. If nothing needs it at logon, delete the Run entry.

rules.title: Machine-wide logon entry has an unquoted path that can be hijacked
rules.subject: {hive}\{name}
rules.why: The command has spaces and no quotes, so Windows first tries each space-separated prefix as a program. One of those locations is writable, so a program placed there runs as whoever logs on next, administrators included.
rules.fix: Quote the program path in the Run value, e.g. "C:\Program Files\Some App\app.exe" /min, and remove write access from the folder named in the evidence.

rules.title: Machine-wide logon program's folder lets non-admins add files
rules.subject: {hive}\{name}
rules.why: Windows looks in a program's own folder first when it loads a DLL. A DLL planted here runs inside the logon program of every user who logs on, administrators included.
rules.fix: Remove 'create files / write data' rights for non-admin accounts on the folder, or reinstall the program under Program Files.

rules.title: Machine-wide logon entry runs a missing program that non-admins can create
rules.subject: {hive}\{name}
rules.why: The Run entry starts a program that no longer exists, in a place where non-admins can create it. A program placed there runs as whoever logs on next, administrators included.
rules.fix: Delete the stale Run entry (from an elevated prompt), or reinstall the program into a protected folder.
